newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Sept 3.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Sept 3.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

ANI on Tuesday reported a 78 percent drop in pre-tax operating profit to A$22.99 million and a net loss of A$213.19 million after abnormal losses of A$198.6 million. The abnormal losses were due largely to the write down of its assets in troubled German environmental engineering unit Holter by A$234 million. ANI also said it was still actively pursuing the possibility of mergers or joint ventures of the Holter businesses.

Executives at National Foods Ltd were not available on Tuesday morning to comment on a report in the Australian Financial Review newspaper that managing director Graham Reaney may be replaced as part of a boardroom reshuffle.
Qantas Airways Ltd said on Tuesday that it was close to finalising a new enterprise bargaining agreement following recent talks with the Australian Council of Trade Unions (ACTU) and other unions.

Equipment hire group Coates Hire Ltd said on Tuesday its 1995/96 net profit was A$10.4 million, in line with the company's listing prospectus. Profit before interest and tax was also in line with the prospectus, rising 10.9 percent to A19.3 million.

News Corp Ltd would pay transport firm TNT Ltd up to A$75 million if News sold its 50 percent stake in Australia's Ansett Airlines before June 2003, TNT said late on Monday. TNT also confirmed that it had signed a deed to sell its 50 percent stake in Ansett to Air New Zealand Ltd, which would generate cash receipts of A$325 million for TNT. News would also provide a further A$50 million capital contribution to Ansett, Air New Zealand said on Monday.

Amcor Ltd said late on Monday it was eyeing an acquisition in Switzerland. It also said it had dropped its target for 15 percent annual growth in earnings per share (EPS). Earlier, Amcor posted a lower net profit of A$338.8 million, from A$359.7 million in 1994/95.
